short_description: Content Manager help - restrict access to records under a divider
description:
Hi team
Our Procurement section recommended we contact you for advice.

Scenario

  *   We are setting up a procurement file in Content Manager for an upcoming engagement. All procurement records must be stored in Content Manager.
  *   For confidentiality, access to the RFQ responses must be restricted to the Tender Evaluation Committee and the delegate. This is for the lifetime of the record, not just while the RFQ is being evaluated.
  *   The Procurement file needs to be used by a wider range of staff; ideally we would be able to silo the RFQ responses under a restricted divider. I wasn’t able to find guidance as to whether this was possible (and if so, how to do it).
  *   At the moment the other option we are considering is to create a second, restricted Procurement file just to house the RFQ responses, but this will separate them from the main records.

Queries

  1.  Is there a way to restrict access to records under a divider?
  2.  What would you recommend?

If you are able to respond by Monday 21 September that would be great, thank you ?

Many thanks
Ilona

short_description: Request to set up SharePoint for the WR Appointments and Legislation Team
description:
Good afternoon

Is your area able to assist my team with setting up a SharePoint site that would be widely accessible to staff within the Workplace Relations (WR) Group?

My team coordinates legislation bids for the WR Group, which involves making documents that legal and policy teams need to work on simultaneously. The issue is that the overarching SharePoint site for the WR Legal Division is restricted to staff within the division (because it contains confidential legal advice). Our divisional EO can grant access to individual staff from outside the division, but we've been told it's not practical for the EO to approve potentially dozens of requests every time we need to collaborate with policy.

Therefore, I'd be very grateful if your area could help us set up a SharePoint site that would be widely accessible to WR Group staff. We would only use this site for coordinating legislation bids and other work requiring legal/policy collaboration within WR Group.

Thanks so much for your help, and very happy to discuss.

description:
Hi Service Desk

Please log an incident for investigation of a Pre-Production ETL deployment failure impacting integration testing.

Environment: Pre-Production (PProd)
System: Azure Data Factory / Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR)
Azure DevOps Build: 879935

During deployment and integration testing of an ETL release in the Pre-Production environment, the deployment failed due to a Java Runtime Environment (JRE) issue on the Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR).

The error indicates that the runtime is unable to access the Java Virtual Machine library (jvm.dll), with access reportedly restricted by an administrator policy.

Failed for PProd Integration Testing, looks like java related issue
 ErrorCode=JreNotFound,'Type=Microsoft.DataTransfer.Common.Shared.HybridDeliveryException,Message=Java Runtime Environment cannot be found on the Self-hosted Integration Runtime machine. Importance: High


CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organisation. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognise the sender and know the content is safe.


OFFICIAL



Good afternoon,



You are receiving this email as you have been identified as a stakeholder for products/applications/services that may be affected by Citrix NetScaler Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and Citrix NetScaler Gateway after ASD issued a critical alert for critical vulnerabilities.



NOTE: For stakeholders who are out of office, this email has also been sent to their nominated contact.



Actions to take



Cyber Security requires you to take the following actions to better understand the risks posed to the department:



  *   Verify whether any products/applications/services you are responsible for utilises Citrix NetScaler Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.
  *   If you are unsure, reach out to vendors or service providers directly to confirm, and CC ITSA@finance.gov.au<mailto:ITSA@finance.gov.au>
  *   Please provide a response confirming whether you are affected, or any actions currently being taken to confirm this.
  *   If you have determined that an application may be vulnerable, please provide as much information as possible. IE will patching occur, if so, when? Have mitigations been put in place? Who is the vendor that you are contacting to confirm the system is not affected? etc



Examples of questions we would like answers for:

Is your system open to the Internet? What actions are being taken to mitigate/resolve? Etc.



Background



The Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre (ASD's ACSC) has issued a Critical Alert - Critical vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and Citrix NetScaler Gateway products.<https://www.cyber.gov.au/about-us/view-all-content/alerts-and-advisories/critical-vulnerabilities-in-citrix-netscaler-application-delivery-controller-adc-and-citrix-netscaler-gateway-products>

  *   Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway products are critical edge devices commonly used to provide secure application delivery, remote access, and access to corporate services. As internet-facing infrastructure, they are frequently targeted by threat actors seeking initial access to enterprise environments.
  *   CVE-2026-19489 is a memory overflow vulnerability. This vulnerability requires SIP ALG (Session Initiation Protocol Application Layer Gateway) to be enabled on a Large Scale NAT (LSN) group configuration.
  *   CVE-2026-19490 is an authentication bypass vulnerability. This vulnerability requires SAML actions to be enabled and/or being configured as a VPN gateway.
  *   ACSC has no information to indicate that a specific industry or sector is being targeted by either vulnerability at the time of this email.



Mitigation advice



ASD's ACSC advises organisations to ensure the following:



  *   Review the mitigation advice on the vendor support page.
  *   Assess networks and environments for the presence of vulnerable versions of Citrix products.
  *   Update affected products to the latest versions and apply patches as soon as practicable (Patches were released on 19 August 2026<https://support.citrix.com/external/article/CTX696939/netscaler-adc-and-netscaler-gateway-secu.html>).
  *   If your Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway products are managed by a third party, such as an MSP or Enterprise IT provider, you should contact that provider to ensure the products have been patched and are being monitored for suspicious activity.
  *   If suspicious activity is detected, notify ASD's ACSC.

Subject: EOI- Japan Young Leaders Program 2027 (Closes COB Mon 7 Sep) [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi International and Research Division,

Are you interested in studying in Japan for one year?

The Japanese Government has offered a unique opportunity to the Australian Government to nominate a representative for the 2027 Young Leaders' Program<https://www.au.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/2022_YLP_School_of_Government_Course_00001.html>. This scholarship covers a 1-year Masters of Public Policy at the Tokyo National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies (GRIPS).

Overview
The Program aims to cultivate national leaders of the future in Asia and around the world. The cohort will include approximately 20 future national leaders from across Asia and some other countries including Australia. Participants gain a deep understanding of Japan, and build the foundations for a network of friendly relationships and improved policy planning capacity among future national leaders. The Department of Education is one of five APS agencies eligible to nominate one candidate for this program (along with DFAT, Treasury, PM&C, and DISR).

Key information
The program runs from October 2027 to September 2028. The Japanese Government covers tuition fees, international return flights to/from Tokyo, and a monthly allowance of 242,000 yen (currently approx. $2,119 AUD/month). There is also an option for subsidised accommodation on campus.

Eligibility
Applicants must be under age 40 (as of 1 Oct 2027), hold a Bachelor degree or equivalent, and have at least 3 years full-time work experience in public administration/APS. The participant would also need to take Leave Without Pay for one year to undertake this program.

How to apply
If you are interested in applying, please carefully read the application information on the Embassy website<https://www.au.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/2022_YLP_School_of_Government_Course_00001.html>, as well as the attached information.

To express interest initially, please prepare a 300 word pitch and CV by COB Monday 7 September to CountryEngagement@education.gov.au<mailto:CountryEngagement@education.gov.au>. Your pitch should outline why you are the ideal candidate for this role, including your relevant experience and achievements. This will be used to determine our internal selection of one candidate to represent the Department.

The selected candidate will then proceed with the remainder of the application (including medical check) by 10am (AEST) Thursday 24 September latest (extended deadline). The Japanese Government will then conduct further assessment stages before announcing the final selection in April 2027.

If you have any questions, please contact countryengagement@education.gov.au<mailto:countryengagement@education.gov.au>. Please share with Education departmental staff who may be interested in applying.


Many thanks,

short_description: Unexpected Passkey Registration Prompts for Staff
description:
We're seeing reports of staff receiving passkey registration prompts across various Microsoft portals.

This appears to coincide with Microsoft's "Passkeys by default" initiative and the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication methods. As a result, users who are not part of the current passkey pilot, or who do not have a corporate mobile device, are being prompted to register passkeys. In many cases, these registrations cannot be completed because passkey registration on personal mobile devices is blocked by default.

Given our passkey rollout is still in its early stages, could we please scope the passkey authentication policy back to the pilot groups only?

Current groups:

AAD_SOE_Security_Key_Authentication
Intune - Pilot - Microsoft Authenticator Passkeys - Personal Mobile

Restricting the policy to these groups would prevent unintended passkey registration prompts for the broader user base while we continue refining our passkey implementation and rollout approach.

short_description: Request to Log Incident: Production and Pre-Production SAP Connectivity Failure Following Certificate Renewal
description:
Hi Service Desk,

Please log an incident for an ongoing SAP connectivity issue impacting both Production and Pre-Production environments.

Incident Summary
Production and Pre-Production SAP integrations are experiencing connectivity failures following SAP certificate renewal activities completed on 27 August 2026. Investigation has identified issues associated with certificate deployment and a change in the SAP certificate chain, resulting in SSL/TLS communication failures between applications and SAP services.

Business Impact

  *   SAP integrations are failing in both Production and Pre-Production environments.
  *   SAP-dependent business processes are unable to successfully communicate with SAP.
  *   There is a potential broader impact to applications that rely on SAP certificate-based connectivity.
  *   Other potentially affected systems include:
     *   EFS
     *   ADMS
     *   CPP

Our Priority Rating
P2 -this is a Production issue requiring urgent attention. While workarounds and investigation activities are underway, the issue needs to be resolved ahead of a planned Production release scheduled for next week.

Current Status

  *   Initial certificate deployment issues have been addressed.
  *   Investigation continues into SSL handshake failures associated with the updated SAP certificate chain.
  *   Diagnostic monitoring has been enabled to assist with root cause analysis and impact assessment.

Affected Services

  *   SAP Integration Services
  *   VSL SAP Gateway
  *   Azure Functions
  *   VSL Key Vault Certificate Management

Incident Reference Please link the Service Desk incident to the following technical incident record for ongoing investigation and updates:
Incident 297858<https://dev.azure.com/lnwgovau/DSD%20Portfolio%20Management/_workitems/edit/297858>: Production and Pre-Production SAP Connectivity Failure Following Certificate Renewal and Certificate Chain Change

Please advise once the incident has been raised and provide the Service Desk reference number for the Incident.

Hi Singh,

I wanted to provide an update on the Graph Connector authentication issue affecting:

  *   EPPIAPP314
  *   EPPIAPP357
  *   EPPIAPP614

Following further investigation, the Graph Connector Agent itself appears to be functioning correctly, with health checks completing successfully on the affected servers.

The issue occurs specifically when selecting "Work or School Account" during the Graph Connector sign-in process. The authentication window opens but remains blank and does not progress to the Microsoft Entra sign-in page.

Findings

  *   Graph Connector Agent health checks succeed on all affected servers.
  *   Connectivity to Microsoft authentication endpoints has been validated.
  *   The authentication workflow reaches the Microsoft AAD Broker Plugin and Microsoft sign-in components
  *   AAD Operational logs show repeated authentication/token acquisition failures
0x80070005 - Access is denied
WS-Trust authentication failures
Failures communicating with Azure AD SSO authentication endpoints.
dsregcmd /status shows:
AzureAdJoined : NO
DomainJoined : YES
AD Connectivity Test : PASS
AD Configuration Test : FAIL [0x80070002]
Client ErrorCode : 0x801c001d

User Device Registration logs show repeated registration discovery failures:
Automatic registration failed.
Error code: 0x801c001d

Current Assessment

Based on the evidence collected so far, the issue appears to be occurring within the Microsoft Entra ID / AAD Broker / device registration authentication process rather than within the Graph Connector application itself.

Could you please engage the Azure AD / Entra ID team to review whether:

  *   These Graph Connector servers are expected to be Hybrid Azure AD joined or registered.
  *   There are any known issues with device registration discovery, Azure AD Seamless SSO, AAD Broker authentication, or WS-Trust authentication for these servers.
  *   Any server registration or Entra configuration prerequisites are missing for the Graph Connector authentication workflow.

I can provide the collected diagnostics, AAD logs, User Device Registration logs, and dsregcmd output to assist their investigation if required.

Please let me know if you would like me to provide any additional information.

Hi Singh,

I have completed an initial investigation of the Graph Connector authentication issue on the affected servers (EPPIAPP314, EPPIAPP357 and EPPIAPP614, EPPIAPP657).

Findings so far:

  *   Graph Connector Agent launches successfully and health checks complete successfully on all affected servers.
  *   Connectivity to Microsoft authentication services has been validated and Microsoft sign-in pages are accessible via Edge browser.
  *   The issue occurs specifically after selecting "Work or school account", where the authentication window becomes blank and does not proceed to the Entra sign-in page.
  *   Microsoft Entra authentication components (AAD Broker Plugin and Token Broker service) are present and operational.
  *   Investigation indicates the failure is occurring within the embedded authentication/browser component used by Graph Connector rather than due to network connectivity or Microsoft Entra availability.
  *   EPPIAPP314 and EPPIAPP357 do not appear to have a detectable WebView2 Runtime installation, while EPPIAPP614 contains WebView2 binaries but the associated WebView process is not being launched during the authentication workflow.

Current focus:
We are currently investigating WebView2 runtime behaviour, Graph Connector authentication dependencies, and any server baseline/security control changes that may have impacted the authentication workflow since the last known working period.
I will provide a further update once the next stage of testing is complete.

short_description: RE: National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) Data Retention query
description:
Hi Julie,

In response to Frankie's questions, we have outlined some general considerations relating to data ownership, storage, and retention/disposal. These are general answers, to give a more accurate answer would require understanding the application of Commonwealth and State / Territory laws onto an example.

One consideration is the potential complexity when involving State and Territory data held by the Commonwealth. The arrangement between Cth and State / Territory for NCVER would require involvement from legal areas.

In any event, here are the general principles:

Data Ownership
The primary consideration is to identify the appropriate custodian of the dataset. Within DEWR, data ownership in the Data Asset Register lists the custodian of known assets within the department. A custodian is responsible for the accountability and management of the dataset. It is possible for an organisation to hold or use data without being the owner or custodian of that data. We have examples of data / datasets hosted internally that DEWR is not the custodian of, eg. CRN is a piece of data we utilise but don't have custodianship of.

In the case of the national VET dataset, clarification would be required regarding whether custodianship remains with contributing jurisdictions or sits with NCVER as the national VET data custodian. There are two NCVER datasets in our Data Asset Register currently, which can be found by filtering on "Data Custodian" (Column G).

Data Assets, Aristotle & Microsoft Purview<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/dewr-rad/SitePages/Data-Assets.aspx>

Storage
Storage solutions and system-specific capabilities sit outside the Data Governance function. DEWR policy requires information assets to be stored in approved systems that support recordkeeping, accessibility, and compliance obligations under the Archives Act 1983 (Cth). We would likely defer to you in Information Management or a technology division for this aspect [Store | SharePoint]<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/SitePages/Store.aspx?isSPOFile=1>

Retention and Disposal
For retention and disposal, we principally take direction from the Archives Act 1983 but there will be specific obligations in other sources, which are a case by case question. Long term preservation, archiving, or disposal will need considerations of legislation, business value, research value, and agreements covering the data. National Archives of Australia guidance on retention and disposal of data and datasets is the best starting point. Whether NCVER assumes responsibility for retention and disposal of the national dataset, the applicability of Commonwealth archival arrangements, and any ongoing state and territory obligations are likely to require records management and legal advice.


  *   DEWR policy is the Record Disposal FAQ: Record Disposal FAQ<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/Shared%20Documents/Forms/QRGs.aspx?id=%2fsites%2fDESE-InformationManagement%2fShared+Documents%2fRecord+Disposal+FAQ.pdf&parent=%2fsites%2fDESE-InformationManagement%2fShared+Documents&TeamsCID=ef30f6fa-9332-407e-be49-bd4d47ace7d5&OR=Teams-HL&CT=1788310493482>

Subject: National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) Data Retention query [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Information Management,
National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) has recently raised a question regarding the long-term retention of historical VET datasets and how information of this nature should be managed into the future.
NCVER is the national custodian of Vocational Education and Training (VET) data, collecting and maintaining data submitted by States and Territories across Australia. NCVER also produces a range of statistical publications, research outputs and reporting that support governments, policymakers and the VET sector.
I have spoken with Richard about the possibility of bringing the NCVER data into the DEWR Content Manager environment as a potential long-term retention solution. However, it is unclear whether this would be appropriate given NCVER's status as an independent organisation and its role as the national VET data custodian.
From both a records management and policy perspective, we would appreciate advice on the following:

  *   What retention, archival or preservation considerations should be taken into account for long-term historical datasets?
  *   Are there archival, read-only or cold-storage options that could be considered where the data is no longer required within operational systems but may continue to have historical, research, reporting or evidentiary value?
  *   Once data has been submitted to NCVER and incorporated into a national dataset, does the ongoing management of that data remain subject to individual State and Territory recordkeeping requirements, or does NCVER assume responsibility for its retention, archival management and disposal?
  *   If responsibility sits with NCVER, could the management of the national dataset be aligned with the Commonwealth Archives Act framework, rather than requiring ongoing consideration of individual State and Territory retention and disposal requirements?
  *   Could NCVER potentially retain and archive these datasets in its capacity as the national VET data custodian?
  *   From an information management perspective, is there merit in a national custodianship model whereby NCVER retains and manages historical VET datasets on behalf of the sector?
  *   If such an approach were considered appropriate, what governance, retention, archival, ownership and access arrangements would be required to support it?
  *   What cost, compliance and risk considerations should be taken into account when assessing the available options?
We acknowledge that some of these questions may extend beyond records management and into matters of ownership, custodianship and legislative responsibility. As such, NCVER may wish to seek its own legal advice regarding any obligations or opportunities associated with the long-term retention and management of nationally significant VET datasets.
Our intent is not to determine a preferred outcome at this stage, but rather to ensure that all relevant considerations have been explored before any decisions are made regarding the future management, preservation or disposal of these datasets.
We are particularly interested in understanding whether there is a more consistent national approach that supports the long-term preservation of historically significant VET information while balancing governance, accessibility and cost.
Thank you for your assistance and guidance.
Kind regards,

Frankie Kenny

One of the components used in the SEMIS tech stack is being deprecated (see below reference). I would like to discuss the possibility of exempting the SEMIS servers from installing Chrome/Chromium 158. Which team would handle these sorts of requests?

Removing XSLT for a more secure browser  |  Web Platform  |  Chrome for Developers<https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/deprecating-xslt>
Chromium-based browsers (including Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge) are scheduled to remove browser-native XSLT support on 17 November 2026. The removal affects both:

  *   The JavaScript XSLTProcessor API
  *   XML stylesheet processing instructions (<?xml-stylesheet ... ?>) used to transform XML into HTML in the browser.
Unlike the .NET 8 EOS event, this is not merely a support policy change. Browser functionality will actually stop working for affected applications when Chrome/Chromium 158 is released, unless temporary mitigation mechanisms such as Enterprise Policy or Origin Trials are used.

This plan is shared by four Function Apps: Inbound, Outbound, Migration and Submission.
The Inbound process is the heaviest workload and currently processes around 145,000 training products in a nightly run.
The current P0v3 plan has 1 vCPU and 4 GB RAM. With all four Function Apps using the same plan and Always On enabled, memory and CPU contention may become a risk.
Moving to P1v3 gives more headroom with 2 vCPU and 8 GB RAM, improving stability for long-running integration jobs and reducing the risk of one workload impacting the others.
This is a scale-up only; no new App Service Plan or architecture change is required.

Subject: RITM0607191 - Investigation Request - Dynatrace OneAgent Potentially Impacting Certent CDM [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Enterprise Management,

I've submitted support ticket RITM0607191 for the Certent Disclosure Management (CDM) system.

From our investigation to date, our working theory is that Dynatrace OneAgent's .NET instrumentation may be interacting with the CDM authentication stack (IdentityServer3, OWIN and HttpClient), resulting in a System.InvalidProgramException during application startup and user authentication processing.

The issue is currently isolated to the Production environment. We have confirmed that:

  *   Production and Pre-Production are running the same CDM version (25.4).
  *   Production and Pre-Production have matching Windows patch levels and .NET Framework versions.
  *   The application configuration and key authentication-related DLL versions are consistent between both environments.
  *   Pre-Production is functioning normally and does not have Dynatrace OneAgent installed.
  *   Production is experiencing the issue and had Dynatrace OneAgent installed on 25 August 2026.

We have also identified references to Dynatrace within the application stack trace:

at System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw()
at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.HandleNonSuccessAndDebuggerNotification(Task task)
at Dynatrace.OneAgent.Introspection.Shared.NewAspNetCoreTracingMiddlewareBase`1.<InvokeAspMethod>d__13.MoveNext()

Based on the above, we are seeking assistance to review whether Dynatrace instrumentation may be contributing to the authentication failure and to identify any known compatibility issues or recommended exclusions for CDM.
Further details, including investigation findings and error information, are available in the ServiceNow ticket.

Subject: RE: Clarification on SharePoint Records Management. [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Pauline,

Thanks for your enquiry.

The SharePoint Support team can provide guidance on SharePoint functionality and storage; however, questions relating to records management, retention requirements, Content Manager, and Machinery of Government (MoG) record ownership and transfer arrangements are best addressed by the Information Management team, as they are responsible for records management policy and guidance within the department.

From a SharePoint perspective:

  *   SharePoint is the Department's preferred product for document storage. Content Manager can still be used in certain scenarios, but these are rare. (see pdf)
  *   SharePoint is intended to support collaboration, document sharing, and day-to-day working documents.
  *   Program documentation such as reports, budgets, acquittals, compliance documentation, and Quality Improvement Plans can be stored in SharePoint where there is an ongoing business need to collaborate on or access the content.
  *   SharePoint sites can be restricted access wise to small number of staff if required to create an area where sensitive or restricted content needs to be stored.
  *   If your area has a particular need for this you should have your own SharePoint site and move away from using a Group or Division wide site.
  *   SharePoint can host documents rated to PROTECTED.  Any documents higher than this need to be in CabNet or other dedicated systems.

Regarding Machinery of Government (MoG) changes:

  *   Whether SharePoint sites are retained, transferred, archived, or managed through alternative arrangements depends on the specific MoG circumstances and direction provided by the relevant business, ICT, and Information Management stakeholders. If required, content can be moved to another Department on another network, however this is very rare. There would be no difference in using CM over SharePoint in this regard.

Kind regards,
Manik
SharePoint Team

short_description: EMT On-Call 19:00-20:00 | Call From Prem Support to Restore a Network Drive for Ministers Office Work
description: Brad Knight called, he had received a call from staff doing work on behalf of the Minister and are missing vital folder and files from \\EDU.application.enet\10000497\<file://EDU.application.enet/10000497/> I called Ops Control, Darryl didn't believe it was his team, I called DBA on-call to ask if this could be a data management task and if so I could then call Iffat. Rose thinks it may be but to call Iffat, I called Iffat and while she is sure Data Management will need to be involved in locating missing files they do not do the restore and thought it was ops control. I called ops control and spoke to Darryl, this time I could provide the shared drive name and he thinks it is done via an application that he no longer has access to and that storage team do have access as well as control access and to call them.  I call Storage and spoke to Thuy, he said he can do the restore, they take back ups with restore points every 30 days. He was happy for me to give his number to prem support to call him to work through it. I reached out to Brad in teams, gave him Thuy's number and he took it from there.  Brad called me back at approx 22:00 to advise it was all done. Tanya (logged in as Iffat had called her) and Thuy worked through it and found missing files. Job closed.

Subject: New FOI request - The Yarn - black coal mining underpayment allegations - LEX 2490 [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Dear Diab

The Yarn has made a freedom of information (FOI) request to the department (attached) for access to:

“I seek access to final substantive documents held by the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations concerning meetings in 2023 with Mr Simon Turner and Mr Sam Stephens about alleged underpayments and employment practices in the black coal mining industry, and the subsequent referral of that material to the Fair Work Ombudsman.

The request is intended to capture the departmental process discussed publicly at Senate Estimates on 25 October 2023, where Assistant Secretary Jennifer Wettinger confirmed that she and Daniel Tracey met with Mr Turner and Mr Stephens, heard their evidence, and that, through the assistance of the Minister's office, the matter was referred again to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Senator Malcolm Roberts also referred to an earlier Sydney meeting involving Mr Turner and Mr Stephens and senior ministerial or departmental personnel.

For the period 1 April 2023 to 31 December 2023, I seek only:

1. Any final meeting brief, agenda, file note, minute or record of meeting for the Sydney meeting at which Mr Turner and Mr Stephens provided material concerning Coal LSL, the Fair Work Commission, the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Mining and Energy Union and/or Chandler Macleod.

2. Any final meeting brief, agenda, file note, minute or record of meeting for the Canberra meeting involving Mr Turner and Mr Stephens, Jennifer Wettinger and Daniel Tracey.

3. Any final document register, schedule, inventory or covering list identifying the documents or categories of evidence provided by Mr Turner and Mr Stephens at either meeting. I do not seek copies of the underlying personal evidentiary documents themselves under this limb.

4. Any final departmental assessment, briefing, recommendation or decision record concerning what action should be taken in response to the material supplied by Mr Turner and Mr Stephens.

5. The final substantive referral or transmittal correspondence by which the matter or material was referred to the Fair Work Ombudsman, including any final covering brief or statement of issues sent with that referral.

6. Any final substantive response, outcome advice, closure notification or equivalent communication received by the Department or the Minister's office from the Fair Work Ombudsman concerning the investigation or assessment that had concluded by 25 October 2023.

7. Any final departmental file note, executive brief or closure record recording the Department's response to the FWO outcome or whether any policy, legislative, regulatory or other follow-up action was considered as a result.

To keep the request manageable, I exclude drafts where a final version exists, duplicate documents, routine scheduling or administrative correspondence, legal advice, personal contact details, and the underlying private evidence supplied by Mr Turner or Mr Stephens. I am content for personal information of private individuals to be redacted where reasonably necessary.”

Responding to FOI requests requires collaboration between the Information Law Team (ILT) which processes and decides the FOI requests, and relevant line areas that hold the documents (or material) and are the subject matter experts. The attached FOI Protocol sets out the role we both play, actions and timeframes to ensure that statutory deadlines are met (the department generally will have 30 calendar days to process an FOI request).

This FOI request is currently due to be decided by 24 September 2026.

The ILT has identified Employment Conditions Division as the lead line area because you are most likely to hold documents relevant to the scope of this FOI request and have subject matter expertise. If this is not correct, please let us know.

Action required by you


  1.  by 27 August 2026 – nominate a contact officer and confirm if you agree with this FOI request being characterised as a significant request
  2.  search for and identify documents that fall within the scope of this FOI request which also includes identifying and consulting with other line areas who may also hold documents
  3.  collate any sensitivities you and other line areas have identified in relation to the disclosure of the documents (including those identified by the Executive and/or the Minister). Your description of the specific harm or damage that would or could reasonably result from disclosure of the documents will assist us in considering whether any FOI Act exemptions<https://www.oaic.gov.au/freedom-of-information/freedom-of-information-guidance-for-government-agencies/guidance-on-handling-a-freedom-of-information-request/legal-definitions-and-questions/exemptions-and-conditional-exemptions-under-the-freedom-of-information-act-1982> might apply
  4.  by 2 September 2026 – provide us with a SES-signed Document Search Minute (DSM) for each line area that holds documents relevant to this FOI request (including your overarching DSM as the lead line area). Documents (and attachments) must be provided to us in a PDF format via the FOI Dropbox (a link will be sent to you granting access to the relevant folder in SharePoint).*

*There is a current issue with converting emails to PDF. Please open emails in Outlook and select Archive Mail. Using open with > Kofax in File Explorer changes aspects of the PDF. A useful Kofax guide to archiving emails in general can be found here: Kofax PDF - Troubleshooting Metadata Issues<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0017428>

  *   Once you have nominated a contact officer to handle this FOI request, we will engage with them and discuss next steps in this FOI request– including what approach to take, how to best interpret its scope, and timeframes prior to documents (if any) being provided to the ILT.
  *   An FOI request is generally categorised as significant where it may attract media or parliamentary attention (or contain other sensitivities).
  *   Throughout this process, we ask that you tell us, if:
o   the requested information does not exist in document format but could be extracted from a database – please do not take any further action and talk to us before creating a new document

  *   executive means AS for non-significant requests and FAS for significant requests

short_description: LANTITE data retention policy – advice on control record requirements and implications
description:
Hi Julie and Phoebe

Thank you for the advice previously provided regarding Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education (LANTITE) data retention (Ticket Reference numbers: INC0513532 and INC0526181).

Our supplier, ACER, has now had an opportunity to consider the advice in detail and has developed the attached draft LANTITE Data Retention Policy based on the guidance provided by your team. We have reviewed the draft and provided some comments for ACER’s consideration. In doing so, a number of questions have arisen regarding the proposed control record approach, and we would appreciate your advice on the implications and next steps.

In particular, while reviewing the draft, I noted that ACER's proposed control record contains a broader set of candidate information than we understood from the advice provided by Information Management. The proposed control record includes candidate name, gender, date of birth, ACER candidate ID and test window information, in addition to disposal metadata.

Our understanding of the advice provided by your team was that “The Department needs to keep a record of the names of candidates so if their information is requested in the future we can provide evidence that it had met its legal retention period and been destroyed in accordance with the Archives Act”.

As the Department has not previously requested, received or maintained an ongoing identifiable candidate-level LANTITE dataset, we would appreciate further advice on the proposed approach and any implications arising from it.

For context, ACER completed an updated Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for LANTITE in 2025 as part of the current contractual arrangements. Legal advice provided to the team was that, as there have been no substantial changes to the project since the earlier assessment, the updated PIA does not need to be added to the Department's PIA register. However, we are conscious that retaining identifiable candidate information indefinitely as part of a control record may represent a change to the Department's current arrangements and would welcome any advice on related information management, privacy or security considerations.

In addition to considering our comments in ACER’s draft LANTITE data retention policy, could you please advise:

  1.  What is the minimum information the Department should retain as part of the control record to satisfy records management requirements?
  2.  Do you see any issue with retaining the additional fields proposed by ACER (for example, gender, date of birth and candidate ID), or would you recommend limiting the control record to the minimum information necessary?
  3.  Are there any information management, records management, privacy or security considerations we should be aware of if the Department were to retain those additional candidate-identifiable fields indefinitely as part of the control record?
  4.  Would retaining this information create any additional obligations for the Department in relation to storage, governance, access management, privacy management or future information requests?
  5.  From an Information Management perspective, what would you recommend as the next steps before the Department agrees to the proposed control record approach?

We are seeking to ensure that the control record reflects both the intent of the original advice and the minimum information necessary to meet the Department's recordkeeping obligations. We also want to understand whether retaining identifiable candidate information as part of the control record could have implications for the Department's privacy, security or information management responsibilities.

Many thanks for your assistance.

Kind regards

Chloe Fang
Senior Policy and Program Officer

short_description: Advice on archiving Knowledge Base Articles in CRM
description:
Hi Information Management Team,

We are seeking advice on the information management and recordkeeping implications of archiving Knowledge Base Articles (KBA) in the Contact Centres' Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Relationship Manager (CRM).

Background and risk
When a KBA is archived in CRM, it remains accessible to staff who have retained a direct link to the article. This creates a risk that staff may continue to access and rely on decommissioned or outdated content, potentially resulting in inconsistent or incorrect information being provided to customers.

Proposed approach
To mitigate this risk, we are considering the following process:

  1.  Save a copy of the KBA in its published state as a PDF

  1.  Retain the PDF as the record of the published article.

  1.  Remove the content from the KBA in CRM

  1.  Archive the KBA so that staff using a direct link can no longer access the decommissioned content.

This approach would reduce the risk of staff accessing outdated information while maintaining a record of the KBA in its published form. However, it would also mean that the archived KBA in CRM would no longer contain its original content.

Request for advice
Could you please advise whether this approach is compliant with departmental information management and recordkeeping requirements?

We would appreciate advice on whether:

  *   a PDF copy of the published KBA is an appropriate record of the article

  *   removing content from the KBA prior to archiving is consistent with recordkeeping obligations and

  *   there are any alternative approaches that would better meet information management requirements while preventing access to decommissioned content.

Thank you for your assistance.

Beth Hancock

Good afternoon,

I'm not sure who the most appropriate person/area is to assist with this enquiry, however, I'm reaching out in the hope that you can either provide advice or direct us to the right area.

While we have an existing SharePoint site, we're unsure whether it would be best to continue building on the current structure or establish a new site to support the future team arrangement. As the restructure progresses, our team name may also change, so we'd appreciate advice on any implications this may have and whether team/site names can be updated later if required.

short_description: National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) Data Retention query
description:
Hi Information Management,
National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) has recently raised a question regarding the long-term retention of historical VET datasets and how information of this nature should be managed into the future.
NCVER is the national custodian of Vocational Education and Training (VET) data, collecting and maintaining data submitted by States and Territories across Australia. NCVER also produces a range of statistical publications, research outputs and reporting that support governments, policymakers and the VET sector.
I have spoken with Richard about the possibility of bringing the NCVER data into the DEWR Content Manager environment as a potential long-term retention solution. However, it is unclear whether this would be appropriate given NCVER's status as an independent organisation and its role as the national VET data custodian.
From both a records management and policy perspective, we would appreciate advice on the following:

  *   What retention, archival or preservation considerations should be taken into account for long-term historical datasets?
  *   Are there archival, read-only or cold-storage options that could be considered where the data is no longer required within operational systems but may continue to have historical, research, reporting or evidentiary value?
  *   Once data has been submitted to NCVER and incorporated into a national dataset, does the ongoing management of that data remain subject to individual State and Territory recordkeeping requirements, or does NCVER assume responsibility for its retention, archival management and disposal?
  *   If responsibility sits with NCVER, could the management of the national dataset be aligned with the Commonwealth Archives Act framework, rather than requiring ongoing consideration of individual State and Territory retention and disposal requirements?
  *   Could NCVER potentially retain and archive these datasets in its capacity as the national VET data custodian?
  *   From an information management perspective, is there merit in a national custodianship model whereby NCVER retains and manages historical VET datasets on behalf of the sector?
  *   If such an approach were considered appropriate, what governance, retention, archival, ownership and access arrangements would be required to support it?
  *   What cost, compliance and risk considerations should be taken into account when assessing the available options?
We acknowledge that some of these questions may extend beyond records management and into matters of ownership, custodianship and legislative responsibility. As such, NCVER may wish to seek its own legal advice regarding any obligations or opportunities associated with the long-term retention and management of nationally significant VET datasets.
Our intent is not to determine a preferred outcome at this stage, but rather to ensure that all relevant considerations have been explored before any decisions are made regarding the future management, preservation or disposal of these datasets.
We are particularly interested in understanding whether there is a more consistent national approach that supports the long-term preservation of historically significant VET information while balancing governance, accessibility and cost.
Thank you for your assistance and guidance.
Kind regards,

Frankie Kenny
Assistant Director
NCVER Policy Partner | Skills Entities and Data Branch | Policy Pathways and Inclusion Division
Australian Government Department of Employment and Workplace Relations

From: BRUCE,George

To: VENKATARAMAN,Krish
Cc: GRAHAM,Clark; SYNNOTT,Trudy
Subject: FW: Domain controlled PowerShell Scripts [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]

UNCLASSIFIED
It is the System Owners responsibility to ensure the security of their systems. This includes the review of code and scripts that may be run to support applications and systems.
IT security is concerned of the uncontrolled use of PowerShell scripts particularly when actioned through unauthorised processes and the potential for damage they may cause to the network. By implementing the requirement to have PowerShell scripts signed will remove the opportunity for rogue or unauthorised scripts to run within our environment however signing does not remove the chance for poor or bad code to run.


Domain controlled PowerShell Scripts
Scripting languages have long been a vehicle of malware on Windows, so PowerShell's security features have been carefully designed to thwart this danger. One of the most common misconceptions is that scripting languages and command-line shells somehow lets users bypass the security protections of the Windows graphical user interface. The Windows security model protects resources-not the way you get to them. That is because programs that you run, in effect, are you. If you can do it, so can a program. If a program can do it, then you can do it without having to use that program.

Risk
A rogue script can act on any domain member objects or systems and the highest risk for this are workstations which have this security feature turned off.

Change
The Information Security Team will implement a Group Policy change to secure these features of PowerShell. This will provide security to be enabled on PowerShell in all domains.

Expected Impact
In implementing this feature will prevent any unsigned PowerShell scripts from working, and prevent any automated processes that have not been signed.

Time Frames
The Information Security Team has approached numerous teams who use PowerShell scripting to facilitate the administrative changes which will directly impact their work and are planning to implement the changes as noted below:

25 October 2012: Development Domain - Remote trusted PowerShell scripts need to be signed by a Code Signing Certificate issued by the Information Security Team. This still allows scripts to be run locally from workstations and Servers.

1st November 2012: Development Domain - PowerShell security to "All signed" workstations and Servers. All PowerShell scripts must be signed by a Code Signing Certificate issues by the Information Security Team. This includes local and remotely run scripts.

8th November 2012: Production Environments - Remote trusted PowerShell scripts need to be signed by a Code Signing Certificate issued by the Information Security Team. This still allows scripts to be run locally from workstations and Servers.

15th November 2012: Production Environments - PowerShell security to "All signed" workstations and Servers. All PowerShell scripts must be signed by a Code Signing Certificate issued by the Information Security Team. This includes local and remotely run scripts.

What you need to do

  *   Identify which teams will be affected by these changes and inform the Information Security Team.
  *   Have a code signing certificate issued and installed by the Information Security Team on nominated workstations and Servers
  *   Have knowledge on how to sign scripts. The Information Security Team will provide one-on-one training to teams who have been identified and issued a Code Signing Certificate.
  *   Ensure affected teams have tested these procedures within the testing environments before the Production Environments have been rolled out. Test systems - if your team uses PowerShell scripts.

For more information please contact the Information Security Team<mailto:technicalsecurityteam@deewr.gov.au>

short_description: Advice request – handling personal information in ministerial correspondence
description:
Hi Information Management Team

I am seeking advice on the appropriate handling of personal information contained in correspondence received by a minister and subsequently registered in PDMS.

From time to time, writers voluntarily include personal information in their correspondence, such as:

  *   Tax File Numbers (TFNs)
  *   Customer Reference Numbers (CRNs)
  *   account details
  *   other personal or sensitive information.

We have historically understood that where a writer voluntarily provides personal information as part of their correspondence (for example, a TFN, CRN or account details), the correspondence should be retained in its original and unaltered form. The correspondence is registered in PDMS as OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and access is restricted to users with a business need to know.

However, a query has recently been raised regarding the Privacy (Tax File Number) Rule 2015<The%20Privacy%20(Tax%20File%20Number)%20Rule%202015%20and%20the%20protection%20of%20tax%20file%20number%20information%20|%20OAIC> on the handling of TFN information.

Could you please advise whether, where information has been voluntarily provided by the writer, should be:

  *   retained in its original form when the correspondence is registered in PDMS, with appropriate security controls applied or
  *   redacted by the minister's office before being forwarded for registration.

Many thanks for your assistance.

Kind regards
Kelly

description:
Hello all,

Home Affairs are seeking feedback on how agencies are progressing with implementing the Data Retention Review recommendations, principles, and guidelines.

For those unfamiliar with the work, the Department of Home Affairs and the Attorney-General’s Department have developed principles and guidance to support clearer, proportionate, privacy-protective and cyber-secure Commonwealth policy, legislation, and guidance where data retention obligations are imposed by government on industry.

Data Branch will provide a response this evening (see attached draft). If you are aware of any actions taken in implementing the Data Retention Review, we would appreciate input so that these can be reflected in the response.

In particular, we would like to hear:

  *   Whether your area has reviewed, shared or applied the materials arising from the Data Retention Review
  *   Whether your area would be interested in further consultation on the implications for DEWR, including with Home Affairs and Attorney-General’s Department representatives.

Please provide any input by 4:00 pm today. Apologies for the short notice

short_description: Advice Required: STP Data Retention and Destruction Requirements
description:
OFFICIAL: Sensitive

Hi Records Management Team,

The Department currently receives Single Touch Payroll (STP) data from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) under a data-sharing arrangement to support administration of the Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System. The data is used to assist with claim assessment and payment verification, targeted compliance activities, and verification of apprenticeship cessation/end dates.

As part of ongoing governance work on the joint data share arrangement with the ATO, I have been looking into developing a proposed STP data destruction approach that would:

  *   Retain evidentiary snapshots of STP information used to support business decisions and audit requirements;
  *   Destroy raw STP data once it is no longer required for operational purposes and any applicable retention requirements have been met; and
  *   Remove replicated copies of raw STP data from downstream systems, including reporting and data warehouse environments.

To ensure the proposed approach complies with the Archives Act 1983 and applicable records management requirements, I would appreciate your advice on the questions below, or guidance on the appropriate area or contact who can assist with this advice.


  1.  Is STP data received from the ATO and used to support:

     *   Apprenticeship incentive claim assessment and payment decisions;
     *   compliance activities; and
     *   apprenticeship cessation/end date verification

considered a Commonwealth record for the purposes of the Archives Act 1983?


  1.  Is this information covered by an existing DEWR Records Authority, General Records Authority, or other approved disposal authority?


  1.  If so, could you please advise:

     *   the applicable disposal class(es);
     *   if there is a minimum retention period(s);
     *   any requirements or conditions relating to the destruction of the data; and
     *   whether destruction of the source/raw STP data is authorised once retention requirements have been met.


  1.  We are proposing to retain evidentiary "snapshots" of STP information used in decision-making (for example, claim assessment snapshots and apprenticeship cessation snapshots) while destroying the underlying raw STP dataset after the authorised retention period expires. Would retention of these snapshots satisfy recordkeeping and audit requirements, or would additional information need to be retained?


  1.  The proposed solution would also remove any replicated copies of the raw STP data held in downstream systems, including reporting and data warehouse environments. Are there any records management considerations or approvals required for destruction of these copies?


  1.  Are there any other legislative, audit, or information management requirements that should be considered when defining the retention and destruction approach for Departmental data (STP data)?

I'm seeking this advice to inform how we undertake data destruction on STP data that has been shared with us from the ATO and ensure it aligns with the Department requirements and Archives Act 1983.

As mentioned if this is not the right team please let me know who might be best to discuss this with.

Thanks
Linda

short_description: Guidance on Secure Vault Solution for Planning Analytics local admin accounts
description:
Hi Cyber Security Services,

I am seeking advice on the department's approved credential management services to support implementation of Treatment T7 from the IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) Plan of Action and Milestones (EC22-008954).

Background
--------------
Treatment T7 requires Corporate Applications to:

1. Ensure inbuilt administrator account passwords are changed on all Planning Analytics databases.
2. Maintain a unique password for each database.
3. Store administrator credentials in a secure vault.

Planning Analytics currently operates in:
1. Development
2. Preproduction
3. Production

Across these environments there are 10 databases, resulting in approximately 30 application administrator credentials requiring secure management.

These are application-level administrator accounts within Planning Analytics and are not AD-managed service accounts, server accounts, or SQL logins.

Could Cyber Security Services please advise:
What approved credential management services are available for storing and managing these application administrator credentials? Would CyberArk or Secret Server be suitable? Corporate Applications would need to be able to manage the passwords of these non-AD local administrator accounts.

Regards,
Elvis

This account will need cloud groups or direct assignments of licences to make it work during emergency.

This request is to establish a dedicated, non-personal Break Glass (Emergency Access) account to support the administration and recovery of critical Microsoft cloud services including,
Power Platform,
Power BI/Microsoft Fabric,
Dynamics 365,
Dynamics 365 Business Central,
Copilot Studio, and associated licensing services.

The account will be used only during emergency situations where standard administrative access is unavailable or impaired, including identity platform outages, administrator lockouts, service disruptions, tenant recovery activities, or business continuity and disaster recovery events.

To ensure full recovery capability, the account requires privileged administrative roles including Power Platform Administrator, Dynamics 365 Administrator, Fabric Administrator, and Business Central Administrator, Exchange Administrator, SharePoint Administrator, Teams Administrator, AI Administrator, Search Administrator and Application Administrator together with the necessary licences such as Microsoft 365 E5 (mail enabled), Power BI Pro, Power Apps Premium, Dynamics 365, Business Central, and Copilot Studio where applicable. The account will not be used for day-to-day administration and will be subject to strict governance controls, including secure credential storage, monitoring, and alerting of all sign-ins and privileged actions, periodic access reviews, and usage only when approved under emergency access procedures.

The account is required to maintain business continuity, enable rapid service recovery, restore access to critical business systems, perform emergency licence assignments, and ensure the department retains administrative control of essential Microsoft cloud Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and it's associated services during major incidents.

short_description: Sandbox will be updated with new OSCA 2024 scheme and training product mapping data
description:
Dear web service users

This email is to let you know that Sandbox TPC will be updated with the new OSCA data on 18 August 2026. This addresses an issue where a number of NRT records were being returned with multiple active OSCA classifications, leading to repeated job failures.

Please note that:

  *   Previously loaded OSCA data will be removed from sandbox
  *   OSCA scheme description and title will change from OSCA to OSCA 2024 in sandbox
  *   OSCA reference data has not changed
  *   OSCA to training product mapping version 2 will be added to the sandbox

This means:

  *   OSCA scheme 2024 will have a start date of 18/8/2026, and ANZSCO scheme will have an end date of 17/8/2026
  *   OSCA to training product mapping will also have a start date of 18/8/2026, and ANZSCO mapping to training products will have an end date of 17/8/2026

Background information
OSCA<https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/osca-occupation-standard-classification-australia/latest-release> is a new Australian Bureau of Statistics occupational classification that will replace ANZSCO. OSCA classifications will be assigned to qualifications, specialisations and AQF?level accredited courses. Full implementation in the production environment is scheduled to be available from 1 January 2027. The ABS will update OSCA in the years following. When updates occur, NCVER will update OSCA reference data and any existing assigned classifications in the National Training Register.

NCVER update on the transition from ANZSCO to OSCA training products
NCVER is in the process of assigning OSCA codes to all nationally recognised qualifications/courses based on their current ANZSCO codes. This information will be available on the National Training Register (training.gov.au) from 1 January 2027. Contact your state/territory training authority in 2027 for information about the OSCA code for any government funded locally recognised courses that you deliver.

Support
If you have any further questions and/or issues, please contact TGA Help<mailto:tgahelp@dewr.gov.au>.

Kind regards

The TGA Project Team

short_description: Dev and Prod Posit Package Manager unable to download artifact, download immediately terminates
description:
Dev and Prod Posit Package Manager hosts are unable to download a specific package, the download is being terminated immediately.  This is preventing JSA Staff from bringing the public-facing NERO dashboard back online:

https://www.jobsandskills.gov.au/data/nero/nero-dashboard

The NERO dashboard has a dependency on an R package called 'data.table'.  R packages are served by Posit Package Manager hosts.

Unfortunately the 'data.table' artifact is being prevented from being served by Dev and Prod Package Managers because these hosts are unable to pull the relevant artifact from upstream source.  The download from upstream begins and is immediately terminated.  

PreProd Package Manager has no such issue and is able to download the artifact from the upstream source, and JSA staff are able to deploy the NERO dashboard application in PreProd.

The URL / artifact being downloaded by Package Manager is:

https://rspm-sync.rstudio.com/v4/1/packages/d65256f0050a6443770d5982b5098a2a8c894f9675ed17053416c7815cbddeb9.tar.gz

I have replicated the issue by using CURL on the relevant hosts to manually try to download the artifact, see attached.

  *   Date: Friday 21 August 2026
  *   Start Time: 2:00 PM
  *   Expected Restoration: Early evening on Friday 21 August 2026
  *   Business Status: Available for normal business operations from Monday 24 August 2026

Reason for Outage

The Corporate Applications team will be undertaking a planned upgrade of the Planning Analytics platform to a newer supported version. This upgrade is required to maintain vendor supportability, improve platform stability, and enable new Planning Analytics capabilities.

Expected User Impact

During the outage window, users will be unable to access:


  *   Planning Analytics (TM1)
  *   TM1 Web / Planning Analytics Spreadsheet Services (PASS)
  *   Perspectives (Excel add-in)
  *   Certent CDM (Desktop client)
Users attempting to access the platform during the upgrade period may experience connection failures, login issues, or unavailable services.
Guidance for Service Desk

If users contact the Service Desk reporting issues accessing Planning Analytics during the outage window, please advise them that:

Planning Analytics is currently unavailable due to a planned system upgrade being carried out by the Corporate Applications team. short_description: JSA CRM - Corporate Services (50038189) - Appointment tracking no User Contact links
description:
'@Samir George / Corporate Services (50038189):
We want tracked Appointments from Outlook Calendar to auto-link to User Contact records in the JSA CRM.
This is not happening currently - can this be changed via any settings?

When we track an Appointment record from Outlook Calendar:
- it currently will link the record to the CRM Contact record of any appointment invitee if their email matches an existing Contact record.
However, it does not link the activity record if the invitee is a JSA staff member with a User licence.
(It also does not link the JSA appointment organiser).

To have the appointment record display in the staff member Timeline/Activities we have to open the tracked Appointment record in the CRM, delete the relevant staff member/User, then re-add them. It will then link to their Contact record.

Is there any way to enable this linking to happen automatically, so that the record links to both User and non-User invitees at the same time when the record is tracked from Outlook to the CRM?

For all affected devices, they appear to be compliant in Endpoint and have had recent contact/check-ins within the last few days.

short_description: FAULT - SharePoint Issue - msg file has asian characters after drag drop
description:
Location Details at time of the call: SA
Best/Alternative contact: (08) 8306 8686
Asset ID: LA338016

Intranet Site / SharePoint Issue

Description of issue: User reports that when dragging Outlook emails to a team SharePoint site, the values displayed in the Subject and Attachments fields change to an Asian language. User is seeking guidance on how to prevent this behaviour and whether the process being used is incorrect.


Troubleshooting/Advice Provided: 
- Characters are only displaying incorrectly in the SharePoint preview of the email. Downloading the email will result in it being displayed correctly
- I advised that this is due to a translation pattern issue and that downloading the email will resolve the issue. Lynda also observed that uploading to SP instead of dragging and dropping results in the characters being displayed correctly

Outcome: As this has only recently started happening I advised I would escalate the ticket to the SharePoint team for further investigation. Workaround is functioning at the moment but client's prefer to use drag and drop method to upload to SP as it is quicker.

Hi Team,

I am reaching out for some help with one of the Sharepoint forms we created that no longer seems to be working properly. After some to-and-fro, I’ve been advised you are the right people to contact. There are two issues we need help with.

Issue # 1:

Group Mailbox: TRADigitalProjects@dewr.gov.au<mailto:TRADigitalProjects@dewr.gov.au>

The intended workflow is:


  *   Trigger: When a new item is created in the list (i.e. when someone submits a form on our Hub).
  *   Action: Automatically send an email notification to the group mailbox.
  *   Purpose: Ensure the team is notified whenever a new request is submitted.

We have attempted to configure the workflow, however it is not working as expected. A screenshot of the issue is attached for reference.

Are you able to please set this up for us or assist with troubleshooting or advice whether there are any permission, configuration, or system-related issues preventing the workflow from functioning correctly?

description:
To: Digital Collaboration Branch (Attention: Singh Talwar)

The FEG Branch is currently undertaking a reporting reform project, transitioning from legacy SSRS reporting to Power BI. To support this work, we request access to Power BI Dataflows Gen2 and Copilot for Power BI. 

We currently experience limitations with Dataflows Gen1, particularly around managing dependencies and refresh sequencing between related dataflows, which increases maintenance effort and can impact refresh reliability. Dataflows Gen2 provides Microsoft's modern data integration capability, including improved scalability, support for enterprise-scale data transformation, and tighter integration with the Microsoft Fabric data platform.

We also request access to Copilot for Power BI to improve productivity across report development and data analysis. Copilot within PBI can accelerate report creation, assist with DAX and semantic model development, provide natural language analysis of data, and reduce effort in documenting and troubleshooting reports. Together, these capabilities will reduce delivery timeframes, improve the maintainability of our reporting solutions, and support the branch's migration to a modern Power BI reporting environment.

Good afternoon, Nadine,

So, it doesn't look like there is anything on Kylie's end and some articles online say Font changes are user profile specific in the Outlook App. I've taken the liberty to write up a little guide for the ways Premier Support would suggest adjusted the hyperlink font. As suspected it seems that copy and paste is copying some of the formatting from the website where the hyperlink is being taken from. The current outlier that's not making sense is when you manually change it in drafts, close and reopen the email it reverts back.

The method we discussed earlier today is as follows:


  *   [cid:image001.png@01DD2672.AC30CEF0] In a new email, once you've pasted the hyperlink in, highlight it and head to the "Format Text" section in the top banner.






  *   Towards the right there is "Change Styles" and a little down-right arrow. Click this to open the styles pop up.
[image]

  *   From here you should see "Hyperlink" as an option, which we can right-click to modify.
  *   This opens a new pop-up box to set your preferred formatting, in this case Calibri. Make sure to click 'Add to the Styles Gallery'.
[image]

  *   This setting now makes that option appear under the 'Styles' section and much more accessible for future formatting, see below:
[image]
So now all you'll need to do once you're ready to send through a draft or format the email prior to sending, is highlight any hyperlinks with the incorrect font/formatting, then click the above and it'll change to your preferred formatting.

After discussing other options with the rest of Prem, we've come up with another option that may work.
As you're email settings are correctly defaulted to Calibri, you can write the desired text, highlight where you want the hyperlink to be placed and right click then go to Link.
[image]

  *   Enter the preferred link as shown in the example below and click okay.
[image]

  *   It'll then insert over the existing text in the default format you've set.

I know this was a lot to read. I just wanted it in writing and a good place to fall back if one or the other option isn't working. If you have any trouble let me know. I'm more than happy to swing by and demonstrate/set up.
